subject: ventures/allergen-label-maker
professional: a food-labelling regulatory compliance specialist for UK/EU (Reg. (EU) 1169/2011 Annex II and Art. 21, FSA PPDS guidance under Natasha's Law) and US (FALCPA plus the FASTER Act); they check first that every named allergenic ingredient is caught, that each allergen is emphasised in the ingredients list with the cereal and nut named, and that a US Contains statement names the tree nut, fish and crustacean species

evidence.correctness: node .../scratchpad/allergen/probe.mjs calc.mjs ran 80 ingredients and 5 labels against Reg. (EU) 1169/2011 Annex II, FIC Art. 21, FALCPA s.403(w) and FDA's Jan 2025 allergen Q&A (from the auditor's knowledge of those texts; not fetched). Right: 25 named Annex II ingredients across all 14 (milk powder, quail eggs, semolina, malt vinegar, soy lecithin, arachis oil, celery salt, E220-E228, langoustine, squid ink, walnut oil, ghee...), maltodextrin exempt, US rye/barley not wheat and spelt wheat, look-alikes excluded in the matrix. Wrong: eight common finfish undetected (sea bream, turbot, eel, carp, skate, john dory, caviar, lox); generic 'nuts' undetected; a second supplier tag silently dropped (soya lost); 'butter [none]' declares no milk; US pine nut/chestnut not declared; label emphasis misses 8 of 11 declared allergen words and bolds 4 look-alikes; US/UK Contains lines use category names. Held at 1: in a user-safety tool the matrix misses named allergens and the label, the headline output, is not the emphasis the law asks for on ordinary input.
evidence.completeness: Matrix, CSV (matrixCsv), labels (labelFor), may=, UK/US switch, supplier tags, customer allergen page (menupage.mjs) all produce output end to end in node and are covered by tests. The label's emphasis feature works only for words in a second list. Browser not driven this round; https://marisstella.app/allergen-label-maker/ could not be loaded (proxy CONNECT 403), so no URL defects filed. No TODOs or stubs.
evidence.verification: cd ventures/allergen-label-maker && node --test '*.test.mjs': 38 tests, 38 pass, 0 fail (189 ms). Six mutations via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (emphasis removed, wheat tag -> gluten, check-dedupe), 3 survived (named-beats-check precedence calc.mjs:165, sulphite E-number range calc.mjs:79, dark-chocolate exclusion calc.mjs:68). No test covers fish breadth, two tags, emphasis of declared allergens beyond 'wheat'/'milk', or US tree-nut species; one test (calc.test.mjs:152) asserts the non-compliant US 'Crustacean shellfish' wording.
evidence.craft: Read calc.mjs (321 lines, pure, no deps), menupage.mjs, index.html module script and the four test files. Good: esc() on all output, JSON in the menu page escaped for <script>, menupage classify kept equal to the page script by test. Defects: emphasise() (calc.mjs:254-281) is a second, narrower allergen dictionary that ignores RULES' 'not' exclusions, so label and matrix disagree; readIngredient uses raw.match (first tag only) but strips all tags (calc.mjs:137-138); noneTag disables named rules (calc.mjs:154); a no-op map in analyseDish (calc.mjs:217-221).
evidence.claims: Backed: disclaimer, no-warranty and 'a missed allergen can seriously harm a customer' (index.html:119, page.test.mjs:7-14); no network calls (page.test.mjs:16-21); local-only usage counting with DNT/GPC (usage.mjs); 'check' never printed as declaration (calc.mjs labelFor uses declaredKeys). Not backed: 'print-ready label ... allergens in bold, the way Natasha's Law asks for them' (index.html:64, README.md:3, llms.txt:3) given the emphasis gaps; README.md:28 '[none] clears guesses' (clears named allergens too); 'the tool uses exactly that' for tags (index.html:102) fails for a second tag; README.md:47 test counts stale. README's 'What is not verified' section is honest about the word list.
evidence.fitness: Job: a UK cafe owner builds an allergen matrix for the folder and PPDS labels for grab-and-go sandwiches and cakes. The example menu works and the matrix is a useful first pass with sensible 'check' flags, but a fish dish with sea bream comes out allergen-free, and every label must be re-edited by hand for emphasis (and for any branded component's sub-ingredients) before it is lawful. A US user gets category names on the Contains line and misses pine nuts. Usable as a drafting aid with a careful human, not as the label.
evidence.domain: Compared with a food-labelling compliance specialist's practice under FIC 1169/2011 (Annex II, Art. 21, Art. 9 compound ingredients), FSA PPDS guidance and FALCPA/FASTER. Sound: the 14/9 lists, sesame in the US list, rye/barley split from wheat, the contains/check/may three-tier design, precautionary labelling left to the user, sulphite threshold explained. Departs: emphasis not applied to every allergen, cereal and nut not named on the label, UK reliance on a Contains box, US Contains without species, FDA 2025 tree-nut list not followed, branded compound ingredients not broken down.

defects.what: Common finfish are not recognised at all (sea bream, turbot, eel, carp, skate, john dory, caviar, lox): a dish with sea bream shows no fish in the matrix, label or customer page, which says 'Not listed'.
Only the first [...] tag in an ingredient is read but every tag is stripped from the text, so 'sauce (stock [celery], paste [soya])' silently loses soya, an allergen the user typed.

Label emphasis uses its own short word list, not the detection rules, so declared allergens (plain/wholemeal flour, brie, halloumi, creme fraiche, mayo, dijon, groundnut, arachis oil, lobsters) are printed unbolded; tagged items (pesto [milk]) appear with no emphasis. FIC Art. 21(1)(b) / Natasha's Law require emphasis in the ingredients list.
US mode never declares pine nut or chestnut, which remain on FDA's tree-nut list (Q&A Edition 5, Jan 2025); they are reported as advisories only.
'[none]' skips every rule, including named allergens ('butter [none]' declares no milk); README says it clears guesses only.
Generic 'nuts', 'chopped nuts', 'nut oil' raise nothing, not even a check.
US Contains line prints category names 'Fish', 'Crustacean shellfish', 'Tree nuts'; FALCPA s.403(w)(2) requires the species / nut type; the test at calc.test.mjs:152 enshrines it.

Look-alikes are bolded on the label (coconut milk, cocoa butter, egg-free mayonnaise, cream of tartar, almond milk's 'milk') because emphasise() ignores the 'not' exclusions, contradicting the matrix.

UK label relies on a 'Contains: Cereals containing gluten, Tree nuts, Crustaceans' line; FIC requires the cereal/nut named and emphasised in the list, and the Commission Q&A says a Contains box cannot replace that.
Headline claim 'print-ready label ... allergens in bold, the way Natasha's Law asks for them' is not backed for the inputs above.
US 'flour' / 'enriched flour' only 'check' though by US standard of identity (21 CFR 137.105) flour is wheat.
Tag aliases miss singular/species names ('tree nut', 'crustacean', 'almond', 'lupine'); an error is shown, so not silent. 'lupine flour' also gets a gluten check.
Three seeded mutations survive: named-beats-check precedence, E224-E228 range, dark-chocolate exclusion.
README test counts stale (says 5 page tests; there are 6, plus 7 menupage tests).

verdict: Allergen Label Maker is a well-intentioned drafting aid with a sound three-tier design (contains / check / may) and a correct mapping of the 14 UK/EU and 9 US allergens, and it catches 25 of 25 ordinary named Annex II ingredients I tried. It does not meet the bar for a user-safety tool: eight common finfish (sea bream, turbot, eel ...) and a generic 'nuts' are not detected, a second supplier tag in one ingredient is silently dropped, '[none]' suppresses named allergens, and US mode ignores pine nut and chestnut. The label, its headline output, emphasises allergens from a separate shorter word list, so most declared allergens are printed unbolded and look-alikes like coconut milk are bolded, and both UK and US Contains lines use category names the regulations do not accept. 38 tests pass; 3 of 6 seeded mutations survive. Fixes are mostly small: extend the fish and nut words, read all tags, limit [none] to check rules, drive emphasis from the detection matches, and add US tree-nut rules.
